clue.text: Disciplinarian marks a test harshly

indicators.note: treated harshly, these three words are roughed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A strict teacher grades an exam severely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harshly' rearranges MARKSATEST into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A strict boss who drives others hard is a disciplinarian.

clue.text: A point we raised once more

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word we is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone repeats a point already made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns WE into EW.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to do something afresh is to do it again.

clue.text: Like a cat's cradle, hard to explain

definitions.meaning: a cat's cradle is a string game full of tangles and loops
a puzzling problem is difficult or intricate

explanation.definitionFit: Tangled string is full of knots; figuratively a thorny, intricate problem is the same word.

clue.text: Article on Rodin's mongrel dog

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: a mongrel is mixed breed, so the letters of the name are mixed

parts.note: the sculptor's name, with the possessive giving no letter

explanation.surface: A piece written about the sculptor's crossbred pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mongrel' rearranges RODIN into DIRON. A dog here is a firedog, the metal stand holding logs in a hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: A firedog is the iron support for logs in a fireplace.

clue.text: A rising market in transport

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word for market is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a mart is a market

explanation.surface: Investors talk of a bull market in transport shares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns MART upwards into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a streetcar running on rails is a form of public transport.

clue.text: New cadet or old soldier

indicators.note: new letters are made from these two words by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Contrasting a fresh military recruit with a veteran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges CADETOR.
explanation.definitionFit: British soldiers of past centuries wore scarlet tunics and were nicknamed for them.

clue.text: Irreconcilable Europeans have to be separated

parts.note: Poles are people from Poland
apart means separated

explanation.surface: Feuding continentals must be kept away from each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: two views at opposite extremes, like the planet's ends, can never be brought together.

clue.text: Official club servant

parts.note: a mace is a spiked club
a bearer is a carrier or servant

explanation.surface: A staff member employed by a golf or social club.
explanation.walkthrough: The ceremonial staff carried before a mayor descends from the battle club.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the functionary who carries the ceremonial staff in a civic procession.

clue.text: It may be produced by carbon monoxide to a degree

parts.note: CO is the chemical formula for carbon monoxide
MA, Master of Arts, is a degree

explanation.surface: Poisonous gas can render someone unconscious.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: deep unconsciousness, which gas poisoning can cause.

clue.text: It's used on watch

parts.note: read once as worn or pre-owned, and again as the pointer ticking round a clock face

explanation.definitionFit: Pre-owned goods are 'used', and the pointer counting seconds sits on a timepiece.

clue.text: What one may say when being shot?

definitions.text: What one may say when being shot?

parts.words: What one may say when being shot?
parts.note: shot means photographed, not fired at: the word people say to smile for the camera

explanation.definitionFit: Photographers ask subjects to say a dairy word so their lips form a smile.

clue.text: Is dismissed but doesn't go?

parts.note: in cricket a batter who deflects the ball onto the stumps is out this way, yet the phrase also means carries on

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, when the ball comes off the bat onto the batter's own wicket, the batter is out; the same phrase normally means continuing to perform.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket term for being bowled off one's own bat, which also means continuing.

clue.text: Derivation of article discovered in French region

indicators.note: the article is found sitting inside the region's name

parts.note: Provence is a region of southern France
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Tracing where a literary piece came from in southern France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered in' is the container signal; 'discovered' tempts as meaning found out, but the pair simply says the article sits within the region.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an object's origin or source of history.

clue.text: Principal finding company in one churchman or another

parts.note: arch means chief or principal

indicators.note: the company abbreviation goes inside the word for one churchman

parts.note: a dean heads a cathedral chapter

explanation.surface: A head of a firm joins a church official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. 'another' defines by pointing back to 'churchman': the senior cleric is another kind of churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior cleric below a bishop is another churchman.

clue.text: Cuts with no sound

indicators.note: the word said aloud matches the spelling of a slang no

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing or no

explanation.surface: Budget reductions are made silently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no sound' splits as a link and 'no' said aloud as NIX.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: small notches made by a blade are little cuts.

clue.text: Two sailors start to eat — sauce required

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
the second sailor, also tar

indicators.note: the beginning of the word eat is taken

explanation.surface: A pair of seamen begin dinner and want a condiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two sailors' gives two TARs.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a mayonnaise relish with capers served with fish.

clue.text: Sort of degree, not even second-best

definitions.meaning: a lower class of honours degree in Britain
ranked below first and second places

explanation.walkthrough: British university degrees are graded first, upper second, lower second and then this class.
explanation.definitionFit: British honours degrees run first, upper second, lower second, then this class; also the place after second.

clue.text: Nearly time to see the moon?

definitions.text: Nearly time to see the moon?

parts.words: Nearly time to see the moon?
parts.note: the moon is seen after dark; and the word for the dark hours is almost all of the compound that adds time

explanation.definitionFit: The dark hours are when the moon shows, and the word is nearly the compound with time.

clue.text: A small number back the church on one occasion

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation for number is turned round

parts.note: no is short for number
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A few parishioners support the church once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NO into ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a single time, formerly.

clue.text: Young fish wife who survived Henry VIII

definitions.meaning: Catherine, his sixth and last queen, outlived him

explanation.definitionFit: Name for a young salmon, and the surname of Catherine, Henry VIII's sixth queen.

clue.text: Go round in a woman's garment

definitions.meaning: to avoid or pass around the edge
a garment hanging from the waist

explanation.surface: Walking round in a dress.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass an obstacle; also a dress-like lower garment.

clue.text: Understand woodcutters made playground equipment

parts.note: to see is to understand
saws cut wood

explanation.surface: Grasping that lumberjacks built the swings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woodcutters' looks like people but means tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: balanced planks that children ride up and down.

clue.text: State crime and motive after trial opens

indicators.note: the word for motive comes after that letter
the opening letter of trial is taken

parts.note: a reason is a motive

explanation.surface: Treachery charged, with the motive given once the court case begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opens' gives T from 'trial', and 'after' puts REASON behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country is the gravest crime against the nation.

clue.text: I've cut the tips for the salad

indicators.note: the word I've cuts into the word for tips

parts.note: tips are ends
the letters of I've, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone has trimmed the ends off salad leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' is the container signal: 'I've' cuts into the word for tips. 'the tips' looks like a cooking instruction to trim leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a bitter leafy chicory plant eaten raw.

clue.text: Vessel is dry docked having another refit

indicators.note: docked means cut short, so the tail of dry is removed
another version of refit, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A boat in dry dock is getting a second overhaul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' removes Y from DRY to give DR; 'another' rearranges REFIT to IFTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a fishing boat using drift nets.

clue.text: Agent works without end

indicators.note: without end means the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a factory is a works

explanation.surface: A representative toils endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without end' drops Y from FACTORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a factor is someone who buys and sells for another, a business agent.

clue.text: A taxi is returning to get us, count on it

indicators.note: returning means the word for taxi is read backwards

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cab coming back to pick us up, rely on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns CAB into BAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of beads on which you do counting.

clue.text: Nymph who faded away normally comes back

definitions.meaning: in Greek myth she pined for Narcissus until only her voice remained
a sound reflected back to the hearer

explanation.definitionFit: Mythical nymph who wasted to a voice; also reflected sound that returns.

clue.text: Frenchman in a grubby vest

indicators.note: the name sits inside these words, spanning grubby and vest

explanation.surface: A French chap wearing a dirty undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a common French male name.

clue.text: The case for the prosecution?

parts.note: case here is grammatical, so the accusing grammar case suits prosecutors

explanation.definitionFit: The grammatical case of direct objects, whose name suggests accusing.

clue.text: Firm work with the pen

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A company deals with writing implements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' is an enclosure for animals, not a writing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an enclosure for poultry.

clue.text: Is bird-watching an appropriate example of this?

definitions.text: Is bird-watching an appropriate example of this?

parts.words: Is bird-watching an appropriate example of this?
parts.note: swap the first sounds of bird and watching to get word-batching, itself a fitting description of the device

explanation.definitionFit: A transposition of initial sounds named after an Oxford don, as word-batching turns into bird-watching.
